items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: I remember the day I got my saxophone of Phil Hardymon, he came into the system, at the Berkeley, California school system. He is the one that handed me my alto.

ctx.x: Thank you. I scarcely know where to start with you because you’ve done so many different kinds of things. And I’m curious if you’ve always had very strong curiosity about all kinds of music.

Yeah. Certainly. When I was younger I started out in Gospel music. I remember the day I got my saxophone of Phil Hardymon, he came into the system, at the Berkeley, California school system. He is the one that handed me my alto. And he passed away a few years ago. A great trumpet player, Phil Hardymon. He is the one who is really responsible for bringing jazz into the Berkeley school system. And so that night I played the saxophone at church. I’m sure I was squeaking and sounding very strange, very much like I…

and no mother. And he couldn’t watch us all the time so I started bringing my things in the house and next thing I know my father got a little looser in terms of the Devil’s music and what I could play at home. And I started playing, I even had the guys over for rehearsal. So that’s how loose it became after my mother had passed away. So I always yearned to play other styles. So I’m playing R&B now, and also, I’m coming from Berkeley, California so in order to play gigs you have to know a large repertoire, also…
